correctness.rationale: Every tree has a unique rung and omitted-rail cut decomposition. Boundary-aware 3-state scoring counts degree-three vertices, and the tree identity L=N3+2 yields the rational GF for all n. At z=1 its simple dominant pole is 2-sqrt(3); implicit derivatives give algebraic mean/positive variance and analytic quasi-powers prove the CLT. The included standalone exact checker exhaustively enumerates n<=7 and verifies recurrences through n=30.

originality.rationale: Three distinct comparisons were carried out: full-text prior rung-renewal law, ladder resistance/tree counts, and general degree-field methods. The prior renewal construction is strong and explicitly acknowledged; no inspected source states the evaluated rational global leaf PGF or both exact Gaussian constants. Novelty is limited to that quantitative evaluation, not the underlying tree construction. Priority may still be preempted by unindexed equivalent computations.

value.rationale: The total number of leaves is a natural global terminal-branching observable, and neither total tree-count recurrences nor rung marginals quantify it. The closed bivariate law yields all exact finite leaf probabilities; the explicit positive variance constant and Gaussian law give predictive fluctuation information for arbitrarily long strips. Nontrivial interaction of cut choices at successive rungs requires the three-state transfer.
